sections.title: Why Orthodontic Practices Need a Different Cleaning Protocol Than General Dental
sections.content: Orthodontic clinics operate on high-velocity patient volume—often 50 to 90+ teen and adult visits per day across an open-bay clinical floor. Unlike closed-door general dental suites, every surface in an open-bay orthodontic practice is visible simultaneously to patients and parents. Debonding adhesive dust settles on cabinetry and overhead light arms, heavy foot traffic scuffs LVT flooring between school-release hours (2:30 PM – 6:00 PM), patient toothbrushing stations accumulate toothpaste biofilm, and parents judge clinical quality within 10 seconds of stepping into your waiting room. Standard office cleaners use harsh bleach sprays that crack chair upholstery and smear chemical haze across clinic floors.

sections.title: Zone 1: Open-Bay Orthodontic Chairs & Clinical Floor
sections.content: Open-bay treatment bays must be cleaned top-to-bottom and clean-to-dirty every night using dedicated Yellow clinical microfiber cloths and fresh flat-mop pads:
items: Chair Upholstery Protection (A-dec, Boyd, Belmont) — Never spray bleach, ammonia, or high-alcohol cleaners directly onto seamless Ultraleather or medical vinyl ortho chairs. Nightly crews disinfect stainless/powder-coated chair bases, foot controls, doctor/assistant saddle stool bases, and floor perimeters while preserving manufacturer upholstery warranties

Debonding & Composite Dust Removal — Microfiber damp-dust overhead clinical light arms, curing-light holsters, cart trays, and lower cabinetry seams where fine resin and enamel polishing dust collects (the #1 thing patients notice when reclined in the supine view)

CaviWipe / Optim 1 Floor Haze Neutralization — Daytime clinical disinfectant wipes drip onto LVT/VCT floors around chair bases and leave sticky, dull buildup. Nightly neutral pH microfiber damp-mopping restores showroom sheen without leaving slippery residue

Touch-Point Disinfection — EPA List N intermediate-level (tuberculocidal) disinfection of open-bay cabinetry pulls, glove/mask dispensers, sink basins, and hands-free faucets with full manufacturer wet dwell time

sections.title: Zone 2: iTero / 3D Intraoral Scanners, Imaging & In-House Ortho Lab
sections.content: High-value digital orthodontics hardware and 3D-printing/retainer labs require gentle, dust-free environmental detailing:
items: iTero & CBCT / Panorex Perimeters — Anti-static dry microfiber dusting around rolling scanner carts, cable trays, and Panorex/CBCT viewing glass without spraying liquid aerosols near optics or touchscreens
3D Printer & Retainer Lab Surfaces — Damp-wipe stone/plaster dust, vacuum-former benches, and retainer trim areas using dedicated lab cloths so fine particulate never migrates back into clinical bays

Sterilization Galley (Clean-to-Dirty Flow) — Sanitize sterile pouch storage and autoclave exterior perimeters FIRST before cleaning the ultrasonic/decontamination sink side, maintaining clear access to OSHA eyewash stations

sections.title: Zone 3: Patient Brushing Station, Restrooms & Teen/Parent Reception
sections.content: Parents choosing between two neighborhood orthodontists make fast trust decisions based on your reception area, consult rooms, and brushing station:
items: Patient Brushing Station — Deep-clean mirrors, faucet aerators, splash guards, disposable toothbrush dispensers, and under-counter cabinetry where toothpaste residue and hard-water spots build up daily
New-Patient Consult & Treatment Coordinator Suites — Sanitize presentation monitors, aligner model displays, glass partitions, and parent seating so every case-acceptance consult feels five-star

High-Traffic Reception & Check-In — Disinfect iPad check-in kiosks, charging stations, gaming/lounge tables, chair armrests, and glass entry doors (removing teen handprints and smudges) using Green-coded microfiber
Patient & Staff Restrooms — Dedicated Red-coded microfiber sanitation of fixtures, mirrors, partitions, and floor drains, plus verified nightly restocking of soap, sanitizer, and paper towels

faqs.question: How often should an orthodontic practice schedule professional after-hours cleaning?
faqs.answer: Most orthodontic clinics seeing 40+ patients per day require 5x/week (Monday–Friday) nightly terminal cleaning, with higher-volume multi-doctor or Saturday practices opting for 6x/week service to keep open-bay floors, brushing stations, and restrooms spotless.

faqs.question: How do you protect Boyd and A-dec orthodontic chair upholstery from cracking?
faqs.answer: We strictly prohibit bleach, ammonia, and harsh alcohol sprays on clinical upholstery. Your assistants handle between-patient clinical chair barriers and manufacturer-approved wipes, while our night crew uses neutral, chair-safe EPA List N disinfectants on bases, cabinetry, and floors.

faqs.question: Can XIRI clean around iTero scanners, 3D printers, and digital imaging equipment safely?
faqs.answer: Yes. Our crews are trained specifically for dental and orthodontic environments—using anti-static dry microfiber around optical/scanner housings and strictly avoiding aerosol overspray near iTero wands, CBCT units, and 3D resin printers.
